key_insight: Rice husk ash can be converted into silica powder that remains amorphous after 800 °C heat treatment but crystallizes into quartz and cristobalite after annealing at 1200 °C, making it suitable for thermal spray feedstock development.
engineering_relevance: This provides a low-cost, biomass-derived route to tailor silica powder structure and phase composition for coating and thermal spray applications.
method: Chemically treated rice husk ash to isolate silica.
Heat treated the material at 800 °C for 3 h to obtain amorphous SiO2.
Annealed at 1200 °C to induce crystallization and characterize phase changes.
evidence_signal: XRD, FTIR, and laser diffraction showed amorphous silica with D50 ≈ 88.9 μm after synthesis, plus quartz/cristobalite formation after high-temperature annealing.
watch_item: The relatively coarse particle size and phase transformation at higher temperature may affect powder flowability and spray behavior, so processing windows need validation.
paper_title: Synthesis of Amorphous and Crystalline Silicon Dioxide Powder Composites from Rice Husk Ash for Thermal Spray Deposit
